screenwriter.name: Story
screenwriter.definition: Plot, structure, premise, theme and setting.

covers.name: Plot
covers.definition: What happens: the actions, events, conflicts and turning points that propel the story forward in cause and effect, unfolding in ways the reader does not predict.

facets.name: Cause And Effect
facets.meaning: The actions and events of the story follow from one another, each turning point caused, so the chain leads to the ending.

facets.name: Conflict That Propels
facets.meaning: Forces in opposition, external or internal, give the story urgency and push it forward.

facets.name: Escalations, Revelations And Reversals
facets.meaning: The turning points that progress the story: problems that raise the stakes, new information that shifts a goal, and reversals of direction and power.

facets.name: Unpredictable Unfolding
facets.meaning: How the story unfolds surprises the reader: original, not predictable, not the standard formula.

facets.name: The Pull Of The Story
facets.meaning: The plot raises a dramatic question that makes the reader want to know what happens next and keep reading, taken on a journey.

facets.name: Goals And Stakes
facets.meaning: What the characters want and what is at risk if they fail, which gives the events their weight.

facets.name: Storylines Across A Series
facets.meaning: In series work, how the plot progresses over a season in arcs and episode storylines, and how storylines are restructured or added.

covers.name: Structure
covers.definition: The framework of the story: how its acts, sequences and scenes are built and ordered so the story progresses from a beginning that starts on time to the climax and ending it builds to.

facets.name: The Story's Framework
facets.meaning: The frame the story is built on, three acts or another progression, used so the story advances effectively.

facets.name: Beginning, Middle And End
facets.meaning: The story holds together as a whole: a strong beginning, middle and end, coherent even when told out of order.

facets.name: Starting On Time
facets.meaning: The story gets into motion early, reaching its inciting incident before setup buries it, and hooks the reader in the opening pages.

facets.name: Climax And Ending
facets.meaning: The story builds to a climax and a satisfying ending that brings it full circle, not one that feels rushed.

facets.name: Scenes That Earn Their Place
facets.meaning: Each scene and sequence is built to move the story to the next, entering late and leaving early, with no superfluous scenes.

facets.name: Pace
facets.meaning: The timing of the action, of what is revealed and of character development, so the story neither drags nor rushes.

facets.name: Built For Its Form
facets.meaning: The story is shaped for what it is: a feature, a pilot or episode, or a short; for a series, a framework meant to repeat each episode.

covers.name: Premise
covers.definition: The idea behind the story, what it is about and its hook: a specific dramatic problem, original and strong enough to start the story forward and to hold up when developed.

facets.name: The Hook
facets.meaning: The idea behind the story, what it is about, strong enough to make someone want to read it and to start the movie forward by itself.

facets.name: Original Premise
facets.meaning: The premise is new, or an original take on a familiar story, set against what has already been made.

facets.name: A Dramatic Problem
facets.meaning: The premise sets out a specific problem: when something happens, someone has to do something, or else.

facets.name: Tested And Dramatically Viable
facets.meaning: The core concept has dramatic potential and holds up when developed; a flawed concept no amount of drafting fixes, and execution must deliver on it.

facets.name: A Premise That Sustains A Series
facets.meaning: For a series, a premise or general story line distinct from any one episode's story, able to generate many episodes.

covers.name: Theme
covers.definition: What the story is about beneath its events: an underlying message revealed through plot, dialogue and image, clear and rich, and about something worth discussing.

facets.name: Underlying Message
facets.meaning: What the story is about beneath its events, revealed through its plot, its dialogue and its images.

facets.name: About Something
facets.meaning: The themes provoke thought, in any genre: the story is about something that might spark discussion.

facets.name: Clear And Rich
facets.meaning: The theme is clear and rich, centred on meanings that engage the writer, and it is where an audience's deeper investment comes from.

facets.name: Dramatised Through Character
facets.meaning: The theme is carried by what the characters go through, not stated: the characters embody the subject and their trajectory dramatises it.

facets.name: Thematic Unity
facets.meaning: The world, the structure and the ending hold to one set of meanings, the ending bringing the theme full circle.

covers.name: Setting
covers.definition: Where and when the story happens and the world it builds: its place and time, its rules and pressures, brought to life authentically and with texture.

facets.name: Place And Time
facets.meaning: Where and when the story takes place: its locale and period, and the sense of place it gives.

facets.name: A World With Rules And Pressures
facets.meaning: The storyworld is defined: its rules, what can and can't happen, its groups and beliefs, and the pressures it puts on every character.

facets.name: Authentically Brought To Life
facets.meaning: The world is rendered realistically and credibly, true to the people and places it represents.

facets.name: Pulls The Audience In
facets.meaning: The world draws an audience in and holds them there.

facets.name: Texture And Atmosphere
facets.meaning: The feel of the world on the page: its texture, atmosphere and tone, and speech that fits it.

facets.name: A World That Sustains A Series
facets.meaning: In series work the world is the returnable element, the engine of many stories, and must be dramatically or comedically sustainable.

covers.name: Characters
covers.definition: The people of the story: distinctive, many-layered personalities with clear goals they act on, who change over the story and whose relationships convince.

facets.name: Distinctive And Vivid
facets.meaning: Characters stand out as individuals, each unlike the others and unlike a type, rather than stereotypes or tropes.

facets.name: Depth And Emotional Core
facets.meaning: Characters are rounded and many-layered, with emotional complexity, contradictions and an emotional core a reader recognises as human.

facets.name: Goals, Stakes And Action
facets.meaning: Main characters want something clearly, have something at stake, and act on it, so they drive the story instead of being carried by it.

facets.name: Consistent And Credible
facets.meaning: Characters behave in keeping with who they are, scene to scene and episode to episode, so what they do is believable rather than convenient.

facets.name: Change Over The Story
facets.meaning: The central character (or several, in an ensemble) changes over the story, at a pace the story sets, through milestones the outline can name.

facets.name: Relationships Between Characters
facets.meaning: How characters bear on one another: convincing relationships, their interplay, and how those relationships develop.

covers.name: Dialogue
covers.definition: The words characters speak: natural and believable, in a voice each character owns, saying little, showing who they are and moving the story.

facets.name: Natural And Believable
facets.meaning: Lines sound like real people talking and behaving, so a reader believes them.

facets.name: A Voice For Each Character
facets.meaning: Each character speaks in a way of their own, so who is talking is plain without the name.

facets.name: Reveals Character
facets.meaning: What people say, and how, shows who they are.

facets.name: Moves The Story
facets.meaning: Dialogue does dramatic work, building the plot and creating tension, conflict or comedy, with no talk that has no purpose in the story.

facets.name: Succinct
facets.meaning: Lines say what they must in few words.

facets.name: Subtext Over Statement
facets.meaning: Characters do not announce what they feel; feeling comes through action and what lies beneath the line, built on what the characters want and what the story is about.

facets.name: Fits The Tone And World
facets.meaning: The way people speak suits the story's tone and setting and stays consistent from scene to scene.

screenwriter.name: Voice
screenwriter.definition: Distinctive voice, innovation and visual storytelling.

covers.name: Distinctive Voice
covers.definition: The writer's own way of seeing and telling, original and recognisably theirs, with something to say, so the script does not feel already read or seen.

facets.name: Original, Not Already Seen
facets.meaning: The script does not feel like something already read or seen: it rises above its genre and the standard formula.

facets.name: A Distinct Point Of View
facets.meaning: The story is told from the writer's own perspective, a singular angle on something human and truthful.

facets.name: Something To Say
facets.meaning: The writer has something to say and an artistic intention, a personal connection to the material that lets the voice reach an audience.

facets.name: Voice In The Storytelling
facets.meaning: The voice is on the page, in how the story is told: the scene description, the dialogue, the characters and the tone.

facets.name: Developed And Confident
facets.meaning: A voice is cultivated over time, honed through scripts and held with confidence.

covers.name: Innovation
covers.definition: A tendency to be inventive, imaginative and to adopt new perspectives: coming up with unusual or clever ideas and new plots, characters and ways of doing things.

facets.name: Inventiveness
facets.meaning: Being inventive and imaginative, coming up with new ways of doing things.

facets.name: Original Ideas
facets.meaning: Unusual or clever ideas, and new and interesting plots, characters and stories, with unpredictable turns.

facets.name: Fund Of Ideas
facets.meaning: Having many ideas to hand, the number counting more than their quality.

facets.name: Beyond The Formula
facets.meaning: Rising above the genre and the standard formula, so the script presents a unique perspective rather than a cookie-cutter one.

facets.name: Creative Risk
facets.meaning: Taking risks in form and narrative approach, experimenting, and risking failure to succeed.

covers.name: Visual Storytelling
covers.research: An ability to tell a story using images and sounds
covers.definition: Telling the story in images and sounds: writing what can be seen and heard, showing rather than telling, so a director and crew can picture the film.

facets.name: Images And Sounds
facets.meaning: The story is conceived and written in the language of the screen, as images and sounds, with its scenes built from actions described that way.

facets.name: Showing, Not Telling
facets.meaning: Feeling and character come through action, description, image and behaviour rather than being stated.

facets.name: Filmable On The Page
facets.meaning: The script gives the director and production team something tangible to shoot, precise enough that they can picture the film, instead of reading like a novel.

facets.name: Cinematic Narrative
facets.meaning: The writing reads as cinema: a narrative that is distinct and cinematic and conveys the mood and feel of the film.

facets.name: Look And Feel
facets.meaning: The intended visual style and visual world of the project, expressed in the treatment and the bible as well as the script.

screenwriter.name: Writing
screenwriter.definition: Writing, screenplay format, synopsis and research.

covers.name: Writing
covers.definition: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience: clear, engaging and concise, conveying feeling and emotion.

facets.name: Clarity
facets.meaning: Writing so others will understand: clear, concise, unambiguous.

facets.name: Economy Of Words
facets.meaning: Saying it in as few words as it takes, developing characters, relationships and several storylines in a concise format.

facets.name: Conveying Feeling
facets.meaning: Using description and dialogue to create suspense, tension, drama, comedy and conflict, so the reader feels it.

facets.name: Showing, Not Telling
facets.meaning: Showing feeling through action and description the camera can film, not stating it, and not writing like a novel.

facets.name: Texture Of Description
facets.meaning: Scene description written with a rich texture of its own.

facets.name: Quality Of Writing
facets.meaning: The overall strength of the writing on the page, judged apart from commercial potential.

facets.name: Audience And House Style
facets.meaning: Fitting the writing to its reader and, on a running show, to the show's house style.

covers.name: Screenplay Format
covers.definition: Laying out a script in the standard, agreed format: scene headings, action, character cues and dialogue on the page, 12-point Courier with correct margins, at a page count readers accept.

facets.name: Scene Headings And Action
facets.meaning: Scene headings in capitals naming interior or exterior, place and day or night, and action that shows only what is on screen.

facets.name: Character Cues And Dialogue
facets.meaning: Character names in capitals set toward the middle of the page, dialogue beneath them, parentheticals on their own line, and speeches broken across pages correctly.

facets.name: Font, Margins And Spacing
facets.meaning: 12-point Courier, correct margins and line spacing, with no cheating of margins to fit more pages.

facets.name: Page Count
facets.meaning: Keeping a script to the length its form and its readers accept: a feature roughly 80 to 125 pages, an hour of television roughly 40 to 70, a half hour 20 to 35.

facets.name: Spec Script, Not Shooting Script
facets.meaning: Leaving scene numbers, camera directions and most transitions out of a spec script; they belong to the shooting script made for production.

facets.name: Title Page And Submission
facets.meaning: Preparing the submission copy: a title page with one contact address, numbered pages, a single PDF, and no name anywhere when a contest reads anonymously.

facets.name: Spelling And Proofreading
facets.meaning: Clean spelling, punctuation, grammar and usage, proofread before the script goes out.

facets.name: Format For The Medium
facets.meaning: Using the format the medium dictates (film, filmed or taped TV drama, studio sitcom, radio, stage) and sending what each form asks for.

covers.name: Synopsis
covers.definition: Summarising a story briefly to give a broad idea of the creative concept, in the short documents that carry it outside the screenplay: logline, synopsis, outline, treatment, scene breakdown, bible and pitch document.

facets.name: Logline
facets.meaning: One sentence, sometimes two, that holds the story's dramatic problem: when something happens, someone has to do something or else.

facets.name: Short Synopsis
facets.meaning: A paragraph giving genre and themes, the forces in opposition, goals and stakes, and the inciting incident.

facets.name: One-Page Synopsis
facets.meaning: The one-pager: the main pitch document, fleshing the dramatic question into characters, escalation, dilemmas and stakes, and for a feature the structure through to the ending.

facets.name: Outline
facets.meaning: A longer document (generally 4 to 12 pages) carrying the major plot and character turning points as escalations, revelations and reversals, in cause and effect.

facets.name: Treatment
facets.meaning: A 10 to 20 page present-tense telling of the film, scene by scene in order, confined to what a viewer would see and hear, conveying mood and tone.

facets.name: Scene Breakdown
facets.meaning: A scene-by-scene prose outline of the whole script without dialogue (the step outline or séquencier), checking every scene earns its keep.

facets.name: Series Bible
facets.meaning: The master document of a series: logline, one-pager, concept and themes, storyworld, format, characters, episode summaries, look and feel, about 10 to 15 pages.

facets.name: Pitch Document
facets.meaning: A short written presentation of a project's concept and nature, used to sell it; once asked for in writing, the WGA counts it as a treatment, story or format.

facets.name: Statement Of Intent
facets.meaning: The note that argues for the project and the writer's connection to it, for producers, directors, broadcasters and funding panels.

facets.name: Scriptment
facets.meaning: A hybrid of treatment and script: prose summary with the key dialogue scenes written out in screenplay form.

covers.name: Research
covers.research: Conduct research to obtain factual information and authentic detail
covers.definition: Conducting research to obtain factual information and authentic detail, using sources such as newspaper accounts, diaries, interviews, books and field observation, before and while writing.

facets.name: Documentary Research
facets.meaning: Reading books, articles, journals and records to gather the facts a subject needs.

facets.name: Research Method
facets.meaning: Choosing the research method a project needs and ranking the possible sources by how useful they are.

facets.name: Interviews And Fieldwork
facets.meaning: Interviewing people, scouting places and observing milieus so a world can be rendered realistically.

facets.name: Films, Books And Images
facets.meaning: Gathering reading, films and images that define the story's visual and sound world and enrich its characters.

facets.name: Authenticity
facets.meaning: Getting the people and the world right, so a reader can tell the writer knows what they are writing about.

facets.name: What Already Exists
facets.meaning: Knowing the films, series and other works on the same theme, so the script stays original and nothing is lifted from a classic.

screenwriter.name: Revision
screenwriter.definition: Revision, taking notes, story critique and critical thinking.

covers.name: Revision
covers.definition: Revising written material, rewriting scripts often several times before a final version, to meet one's own standards and the needs of producers and directors while keeping the project's coherence.

facets.name: Rewrite
facets.meaning: Significant changes in plot, story line or the relationships of characters, going to the root of the drama.

facets.name: Polish
facets.meaning: Changes in dialogue, narration or action that stop short of a rewrite.

facets.name: Finding What To Rewrite
facets.meaning: Analysing one's own draft to find the lines of rewriting, through to the shooting version.

facets.name: Revising From Notes
facets.meaning: Rewriting in response to artistic, budget and technical notes, judged on the quality of the revised script.

facets.name: Keeping Coherence
facets.meaning: Producing a new version that keeps the original project's singularity and coherence, without superficial changes for their own sake.

facets.name: Drafts On Deadline
facets.meaning: Turning drafts around quickly and creatively, a first, second and third draft to agreed deadlines.

facets.name: Production Rewrites
facets.meaning: Revising the script in response to budget and casting decisions and solving script problems during the shoot.

facets.name: Knowing When A Draft Is Done
facets.meaning: The writer decides when a draft is finished and delivers it, rather than revising on and on for free.

covers.name: Taking Notes
covers.definition: Taking feedback from producers, script editors and peers constructively and without defensiveness, finding the problem behind each note, and answering it with comprehensive solutions in the next draft.

facets.name: Listening And Clarifying
facets.meaning: Listening, asking for clarification, and answering a set of notes by saying which are clear and which need more.

facets.name: Openness Without Defensiveness
facets.meaning: Welcoming positive and negative feedback and responding constructively, clearly and respectfully.

facets.name: Diagnosing The Note
facets.meaning: Finding what is really causing the problem a note points at, and how best to treat it.

facets.name: Holding Your Take
facets.meaning: Not saying yes to every note: explaining why one doesn't work and arguing for creative decisions.

facets.name: Addressing Notes
facets.meaning: Acting on the notes: reconsidering the approach and carrying the answers into the next version.

facets.name: Seeking Feedback
facets.meaning: Getting feedback from producers, script editors, actors and everyone in the room, whatever their title.

covers.name: Story Critique
covers.definition: Reading a script, synopsizing it and evaluating its strengths and weaknesses (its story, characters, dialogue and world), then critiquing it constructively with ways to improve it.

facets.name: Synopsizing
facets.meaning: Summarising the material at the head of coverage: a thumbnail sketch of the story.

facets.name: Strengths And Weaknesses
facets.meaning: Weighing the pros and cons of the subject, story, characters, dialogue and visual and sound world.

facets.name: Dramaturgical Analysis
facets.meaning: Checking the story's coherence against the author's intention: acts, point of view, character construction, the audience's place.

facets.name: Judging Potential
facets.meaning: Estimating whether the material is worth developing or acquiring: its format, genre, audience and possible funders.

facets.name: Constructive Notes
facets.meaning: Turning the analysis into clear, respectful creative and structural notes with ways forward.

facets.name: Tracking Drafts
facets.meaning: Once a project is in development, comparing drafts to track changes, note improvements and suggest next steps.

facets.name: Breadth Of Reference
facets.meaning: Knowing films and scripts of every genre and period, bad ones included, to see how the page becomes the screen.

covers.name: Critical Thinking
covers.definition: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems, and thinking through new concepts well enough to convey them in writing.

facets.name: Weighing Alternatives
facets.meaning: Identifying the strengths and weaknesses of the possible approaches and choosing the most appropriate.

facets.name: Solving Complex Problems
facets.meaning: Identifying a complex problem, reviewing what bears on it, and developing and evaluating options.

facets.name: Grasping New Concepts
facets.meaning: Thinking through or understanding new concepts, and conveying them through writing.

facets.name: Evaluating Own And Others' Work
facets.meaning: Judging the aims, success or failure of one's own scripts and others'.

facets.name: Analytical Ability
facets.meaning: Analytical ability with an awareness of structure, and a gift for observation and reflection.

covers.name: Time Management
covers.definition: Managing one's own time and the time of others, following a work schedule so drafts and story documents are delivered on agreed deadlines.

facets.name: Meeting Deadlines
facets.meaning: Delivering drafts, rewrites and story documents on the dates agreed.

facets.name: Planning The Writing
facets.meaning: Organising a commission's stages (synopsis, treatment, step outline, script) and the writing schedule with rigour.

facets.name: Realistic Timelines
facets.meaning: Setting timelines one can keep and keeping producers and executives updated along the way.

facets.name: Several Projects At Once
facets.meaning: Working on several projects simultaneously, on long film timescales and shorter television ones.

facets.name: Prolific Output
facets.meaning: Producing a high volume of pages.

covers.name: Perseverance
covers.definition: Determination and resolve to complete tasks in the face of difficult circumstances, on projects that can take years, holding up when problems come.

facets.name: Determination
facets.meaning: Persisting and staying determined through obstacles.

facets.name: Seeing Long Projects Through
facets.meaning: Completing complex projects that can take years.

facets.name: Resilience
facets.meaning: Holding up when problems and difficulties come.

facets.name: Self-Discipline
facets.meaning: Driving one's own work with self-discipline and personal motivation.

screenwriter.name: Pitching
screenwriter.definition: Pitching, promotion, persuasion, speaking, networking, social perceptiveness and film production process.

covers.name: Pitching
covers.definition: Presenting your story ideas and screenplays to buyers (producers, film and television executives, agents and managers), aloud and in pitch documents, to win their interest.

facets.name: Preparing The Pitch
facets.meaning: Doing the homework before the room: learning the project's history, the competition and what the buyers want, reading the material, and rehearsing the pitch aloud against the clock.

facets.name: Presenting The Story Aloud
facets.meaning: Telling the story and its intentions out loud, briefly and in order, bringing out its strengths and what makes it singular, so the listener grasps it at once.

facets.name: The Take
facets.meaning: Finding what the story is really about, its core way in, and shaping a take that meets the buyers' expectations while feeling uniquely your own.

facets.name: Why You
facets.meaning: Showing what connects you to the material, so the buyer believes you are the writer for it.

facets.name: Pitch Documents
facets.meaning: The written side of a pitch: the pitch outline or document, the deck, the series bible and the statement of intent, and knowing that leaving such material behind unpaid is free work the MBA prohibits.

facets.name: Feedback On The Pitch
facets.meaning: Taking the listeners' feedback and questions on a pitch and working their notes into it rather than ignoring them.

covers.name: Promotion
covers.definition: Promoting your work and yourself as a writer to professionals and the public: getting scripts to producers and directors, talking about the work at events, festivals and readings, and finding new clients.

facets.name: Getting The Script Out
facets.meaning: Promoting an original screenplay to producers and directors and seeking backers and financial partners for it.

facets.name: Talking About The Work
facets.meaning: Talking about your work in public: at meetings, workshops and debates, in readings and speeches.

facets.name: Festivals
facets.meaning: Taking part in film festivals to promote projects.

facets.name: Publicity For The Film
facets.meaning: Taking part in the publicity of a produced film: the press junket, the press kit and the premiere, which the MBA gives the writer a right to.

facets.name: Getting Noticed
facets.meaning: Getting yourself noticed and finding new clients and readers: through competitions, social media and other writers and industry professionals, and by citing competition placements.

facets.name: Promotional Documents
facets.meaning: Writing the documents that sell a project to partners: the series bible as a promotion document, the pitch and the statement of intent.

covers.name: Persuasion
covers.definition: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior: arguing a creative point, influencing and winning people over, resolving differences in professional opinions and negotiating.

facets.name: Changing Minds
facets.meaning: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior, and convincing listeners to buy into an idea.

facets.name: Arguing A Creative Point
facets.meaning: Standing up for your creative choices: explaining respectfully why a note doesn't work, saying what matters most to you, and pitching what you think is best rather than what you think they want to hear.

facets.name: Winning People Over
facets.meaning: Influencing the people in the room, buyers and fellow writers alike, so they come on board with your idea and with you.

facets.name: Reaching Common Ground
facets.meaning: Bringing differing opinions together, as in a story meeting, and reconciling them into a common ground.

facets.name: Negotiating The Deal
facets.meaning: Negotiating your own deal, with your representatives, above the guild minimums: compensation, bonuses and other deal points.

covers.name: Speaking
covers.definition: Talking to others to convey information effectively, expressing ideas in speech, clearly, so others will understand.

facets.name: Getting Ideas Across
facets.meaning: Communicating information and ideas in speech so others understand them.

facets.name: Speaking Clearly
facets.meaning: Speaking clearly enough that others can understand you.

facets.name: In Meetings
facets.meaning: Speaking for yourself and your work with producers, executives, directors and your reps: presenting yourself and your projects, giving a coherent account of your intentions, and keeping communication open.

facets.name: Speaking To An Audience
facets.meaning: Giving a talk or presentation in which a piece of work or an idea is shown and explained to an audience, from a reading to a pitch on a stage.

covers.name: Networking
covers.definition: Reaching out to and meeting people in the industry, above all agents and producers, and building and keeping those relationships for mutual benefit.

facets.name: Meeting Agents And Producers
facets.meaning: Getting in front of the people who commission writing (agents, producers, directors, showrunners, broadcasters) in meetings, including the general meeting.

facets.name: Keeping In Touch
facets.meaning: Maintaining contacts over time: following up when invited to, keeping track of what people are doing, leaving every meeting with an open line, and not burning bridges.

facets.name: Fellow Writers
facets.meaning: A network among fellow writers and peers at the same level, met in rooms, roundtables and programmes, who lean on and recommend each other.

facets.name: Everyone In The Room
facets.meaning: Treating everyone you meet, whatever their title, as part of your network, since today's assistants become tomorrow's buyers.

facets.name: Festivals And Events
facets.meaning: Going to festivals, conferences and their events to meet the industry and put projects in front of it.

facets.name: Working Your Reps
facets.meaning: Using your agent or manager actively: telling them what you need, asking for introductions to their other clients and for submissions on projects.

covers.name: Social Perceptiveness
covers.definition: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

facets.name: Reading Reactions
facets.meaning: Noticing how others react and understanding why they react as they do.

facets.name: Reading Buyers
facets.meaning: Understanding why producers and executives want what they want, what pressures they are under, and what lies behind their notes.

facets.name: Reading The Audience
facets.meaning: Understanding how an audience, from readers to a pitch panel, reacts to certain ideas, so as to connect with it.

covers.name: Film Production Process
covers.definition: Knowing the stages of making a film or programme (scriptwriting, financing, shooting, editing and distribution), the trades the script passes through, and what it costs.

facets.name: Stages Of Production
facets.meaning: The development stages from script through financing, shooting and editing to distribution.

facets.name: Production Departments
facets.meaning: Camera, directing, design, costume, lighting, editing and sound, and how each trade meets the writer's job.

facets.name: What A Script Costs
facets.meaning: Knowing the financial impact of storylines, cast and effects, and estimating a budget to check the project is feasible.

facets.name: The Writer In Production
facets.meaning: Where the writer comes in once the script is made: meeting the director, the cast reading, the set, the cuts.

producer.name: Development
producer.definition: Select plays, scripts, books, news content, or ideas to be produced, Securing rights and initial funding, Obtain rights to scripts or to such items as existing video footage, Commissioning preferences and tariffs, Balance creative ambition with real-world demands, Creativity and Pitch ideas to TV companies and film studios to back your project.

covers.name: Select plays, scripts, books, news content, or ideas to be produced
covers.research: Select plays, scripts, books, news content, or ideas to be produced
covers.definition: Choosing which plays, scripts, books or ideas get produced: finding the material, judging the story and its artistic and commercial potential, fitting it to the company's artistic policy, and choosing the script and its writer.

facets.name: Finding Material
facets.meaning: Searching out the source material, story ideas and intellectual property a project can be built on.

facets.meaning: Informing and entertaining in written, oral and visual form, with coherent visual and auditory communication.

facets.name: Fitting The Platform
facets.meaning: Adapting the work to the type of media and platform, and knowing how the industry's forms are changing.

facets.name: Keeping Watch On The Industry
facets.meaning: Following artistic, technical and industry trends and studying media sources for ideas.
judges: France compétences RNCP40926 professional jury (Concepteur - Réalisateur audiovisuel et cinématographique)

facets.name: Reaching The Audience
facets.meaning: Planning how the work reaches its audience, and communicating with the trade, the media and the public.
judges: Telefilm Talent to Watch, AFCOOP peer jury

actor.name: Acting
actor.definition: Acting techniques, Understanding character and situation, Text analysis, Own interpretation, Research roles, Study roles from scripts, Contrasting range (classical and contemporary), Flexibility across genres and styles, Shakespeare and Individuality.

covers.name: Acting techniques
covers.definition: The techniques actors use to build lifelike performances, from Stanislavski, Brecht, the Method and Meisner to Chekhov and Laban, applied to suit the tone and style of the work.

facets.name: Named Methods
facets.meaning: Knowing and practising the established methods: Stanislavski, the Method, Meisner, Chekhov, Laban, Viewpoints, Brecht.

facets.name: Fitting Technique To The Work
facets.meaning: Choosing and applying the technique that suits the context, so the performance delivers the tone and style of the piece.
judges: NIDA BFA (Acting)

facets.name: Your Own Process
facets.meaning: Testing approaches without dogma until you have a working process of your own.

facets.name: Integrated Technique
facets.meaning: Practising a range of effective techniques until they are integrated into the work.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting assessment criteria

facets.name: Work On Self, Role And Ensemble
facets.meaning: Technique as work on oneself, on the role and within the ensemble.

covers.name: Understanding character and situation
covers.definition: Grasping who the character is, their circumstances, whom they speak to and why, from a reading of the whole play, and conveying it.

facets.name: Reading The Whole Play
facets.meaning: Reading the entire play a speech or scene comes from, so the character and context are understood.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines)

facets.name: Who, Where And To Whom
facets.meaning: Knowing the given circumstances: whom the character is speaking to, where they are, and why.
judges: Juilliard Drama Division faculty (Actor Training Program audition)

facets.name: What The Character Wants
facets.meaning: The character's need and what they are trying to achieve, the stakes of the situation, and where the speech changes direction.

facets.name: Subtext
facets.meaning: Investigating character in complex dramatic situations and working with subtext, kept through a story shot out of order.

facets.name: Conveying It
facets.meaning: Showing that understanding in the audition, through deep familiarity with the text, which a panel notes in scene study.
judges: RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (full workshop day, scene study)
USC School of Dramatic Arts BFA pre-screen

covers.name: Text analysis
covers.definition: Reading, understanding and analysing a play's text, its meaning, structure and emotional registers, and basing acting choices on that analysis.

facets.name: Meaning, Structure And Emotional Register
facets.meaning: Decoding what the work means, how it is built, and the emotional registers it moves through.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien assessment (RNCP38358)

facets.name: The Language As Instructions
facets.meaning: Reading the text's construction, its punctuation, rhetoric, rhythms and literary devices, as the writer's instructions for how it is played.

facets.name: Analysis Into Acting Choices
facets.meaning: Turning the analysis into informed acting choices and an active part in interpreting the production.
judges: RADA BA Acting (Hons) module assessment

facets.name: Judging The Play
facets.meaning: Analysing a play perceptively and evaluating it critically, ready to tell a director what one thinks of it.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines)

facets.name: Sight-Reading
facets.meaning: Reading a text aloud fluently at first sight, which the voice panel notes at audition.
judges: RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (full workshop day, voice)

covers.name: Own interpretation
covers.definition: Building one's own reading of a role from the work and the director's instructions, and playing it in one's own way, not copying another performance.

facets.name: Proposing Acting Choices
facets.meaning: Proposing and refining lines of interpretation, built from the work and from the direction given.

facets.name: Original, Not Copied
facets.meaning: Performing the piece one's own way, not mimicking another performance or a teacher's reading, so the panel sees the actual person.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting audition panel
RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (speech choice, on its list of things not to do)

facets.name: Imaginative Connection
facets.meaning: An imaginative response to the text and character, and a personal artistic response: what the actor wants to say through the material.
judges: RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (full workshop day, speeches)

covers.name: Research roles
covers.definition: Researching the historical background and artistic concept of a play, and the social and cultural world of a role, to understand its parts, themes and characters.

facets.name: Historical, Social And Cultural Background
facets.meaning: Working out the history, social world and culture behind the play and each role.

facets.name: Parts, Themes And Characters
facets.meaning: Research aimed at understanding the parts, the themes and how the characters are drawn.

facets.name: Personal Dramaturgical Research
facets.meaning: One's own dramaturgical research, building a body of documents, which a drama school asks to see written up in a production journal.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School assessment (MFA, final term)
Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien assessment (RNCP38358)

facets.name: Researching The Production
facets.meaning: Before an audition, finding out about the production, its creative team and the role.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines), musical theatre

covers.name: Study roles from scripts
covers.definition: Studying and rehearsing a role from the script to interpret it, learning its lines, stunts and cues as directed.

facets.name: Lines, Stunts And Cues
facets.meaning: The script study that underlies the role: interpreting it and learning its lines, stunts and cues, as the director sets them.

facets.name: Lines, Gestures And Expressions
facets.meaning: Studying and rehearsing the gestures and expressions of the role along with its text.

facets.name: Self-Study Of The Role
facets.meaning: Getting to know the role alone before rehearsal, so the actor is familiar enough with the material not to be buried in the script.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines)

facets.name: Research, Analyse, Learn
facets.meaning: Role study as a sequence: research the background, read and analyse the text, then learn it by heart.

covers.name: Contrasting range (classical and contemporary)
covers.definition: Showing range through contrasting pieces: classical and contemporary, dramatic and comic, serious and light.

facets.name: Contrast Of Tone
facets.meaning: Pieces that contrast in tone, dramatic and comic, serious and light, active and reflective, or in character, so the panel can judge acting potential.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School audition panel (stage 1 self-tape)
RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (stage 1 self-tape)

facets.name: Classical And Contemporary
facets.meaning: One piece from the classical repertoire and one modern, each school drawing the line at its own date (1900, 1960, 1980).
judges: CNSAD entrance jury (concours 1er cycle)
National Theatre School of Canada Acting audition
USC School of Dramatic Arts BFA pre-screen

facets.name: Different Sides Of Yourself
facets.meaning: Characters chosen so each brings out a different side of the actor and shows a capacity for transformation.
judges: Juilliard Drama Division faculty (Actor Training Program audition)

facets.name: Pieces In Reserve
facets.meaning: A third and fourth contrasting piece learned and ready, for when the panel asks for more or a later round requires it.
judges: David Geffen School of Drama at Yale, Acting Audition Committee
Guildhall School BA Acting audition panel (second round)

covers.name: Flexibility across genres and styles
covers.definition: Adapting to different roles, genres and styles, ways of acting and aesthetics, and to different performance contexts.

facets.name: Styles, Modes And Aesthetics
facets.meaning: Serving the range of the repertoire: its styles, modes of acting and aesthetics.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien assessment (RNCP38358)

facets.name: Period And Genre Demands
facets.meaning: Knowing what the acting styles of the major periods and genres demand, from psychological realism and epic theatre to commedia and form-conscious play.

facets.name: Convincing Across Genres
facets.meaning: Creating characters convincingly across genres and styles, with other actors, including casting beyond one’s usual range.
judges: RADA BA Acting (Hons) module assessment

facets.name: Across Stage, Screen And Audio
facets.meaning: Carrying the craft across performance media, stage, screen and recorded audio.

covers.name: Shakespeare
covers.definition: Performing Shakespeare and other heightened classical text, much of it verse, in which language drives the action.

facets.name: The Classical Speech
facets.meaning: A speech from Shakespeare or his contemporaries, asked at several drama-school auditions and at RSC casting meetings; Guildhall no longer requires one.
judges: Juilliard Drama Division faculty (Actor Training Program audition)
RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (stages 1 and 2)
Royal Shakespeare Company casting team (local actors’ general meetings)

facets.name: Language Drives The Action
facets.meaning: Heightened text lifts beyond everyday speech: language is the engine of the action and the character's need is pursued through image-laden words.
judges: Juilliard Drama Division faculty (Actor Training Program audition)

facets.name: Speaking Verse
facets.meaning: Performing effectively in verse, its rhythm, structure and line, which several auditions require.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting audition panel (first round)

facets.name: Your Natural Voice
facets.meaning: Speaking the classical speech in one’s natural voice rather than a put-on one.
judges: RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (speech choice)

facets.name: Classical Roles On Stage
facets.meaning: Shakespeare played in performance, in training projects and productions, and in classical stage roles that an award for young actors recognises.
judges: Ian Charleson Awards (as reported by RADA)
Ian Charleson Awards (as reported by WhatsOnStage)

covers.name: Individuality
covers.definition: A strong sense of who you are as an artist, your heart, your own way and your unique voice, which auditions look for and training develops rather than restricts.

facets.name: A Strong Sense Of Self
facets.meaning: Being at home with yourself, with a strong sense of individuality.
judges: Yale (David Geffen School of Drama) Acting Admissions Committee

facets.name: Your Own Way
facets.meaning: Doing the work your own way, not a teacher's or a friend's interpretation.
judges: Guildhall School acting audition panel

facets.name: Material That Reveals You
facets.meaning: Choosing pieces that reveal something personal and your own idea of acting.

facets.name: Artistic Identity
facets.meaning: Developing and affirming your individual artistic identity and unique voice.

facets.name: Individual Within The Ensemble
facets.meaning: Keeping your individuality and unique voice while working in the group.

facets.name: Standing Out To Casting
facets.meaning: Conveying what is unique about you so casting notices.

covers.name: Memorise lines
covers.definition: Learning a role by heart, whether text, movement or music, so it can be played without the script.

facets.name: Text, Moves And Music
facets.meaning: What is learned by heart is the whole role: the lines, but also the movement, stunts, cues and music.

facets.name: Off-Book When It Counts
facets.meaning: Drama-school auditions want every piece fully memorised; casting directors do not expect a first meeting off-book but do expect it at final recalls and prefer it on tape.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines), musical theatre
Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines), self-tapes
David Geffen School of Drama at Yale, Acting Audition Committee
Juilliard Drama Division faculty (Actor Training Program audition)

facets.name: Word-Perfect
facets.meaning: Speaking the lines as written, without paraphrase or added fillers, above all in a classical piece or with the writer in the room.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines)

facets.name: Pages In The Time Given
facets.meaning: How much must be learned and how fast: for a first self-tape, at most six pages, with four days to learn them, or three days for three pages or fewer.
judges: Casting directors under Equity's self-tape guidance

facets.name: Line-Learning Technique
facets.meaning: Learning a role as a practised technique, worked on in class and in self-directed study, and attested by the French actor diplomas.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien assessment (RNCP38358)

covers.name: Memorization
covers.definition: The ability to remember information such as words, numbers, pictures, and procedures.

facets.name: Recall
facets.meaning: A good memory: retaining words, numbers, pictures and procedures and bringing them back when needed.

facets.name: Taking It In
facets.meaning: A strong capacity to take in material and keep it, with the stamina for hard role texts, repetition and long waits on set.

facets.name: Keeping The Memory Trained
facets.meaning: Developing memorising techniques and processes and keeping them up, which the French actor diploma attests.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien assessment (RNCP38358)

covers.name: Konzentrationsfähigkeit
covers.definition: The ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time without being distracted, kept up with concentration techniques, on stage, on set and in the audition room.

facets.name: Sustained Attention
facets.meaning: Concentrating over time without being distracted.
judges: O*NET 27-2011.00 Actors

facets.name: Concentration Techniques
facets.meaning: Mastering and applying techniques of concentration as part of the craft.

facets.name: Energy And Concentration On Set
facets.meaning: Managing energy and concentration through the technical demands of a set.

facets.name: Focus In The Audition
facets.meaning: Concentrating on giving a good audition rather than on remembering lines.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting audition panels

actor.name: Voice
actor.definition: Accents and dialects, Speak different languages, Voice-over (incl. home studio), Singing and Speaking.

covers.name: Accents and dialects
covers.definition: The accents and dialects an actor can do convincingly, beginning with their own native accent.

facets.name: Your Own Accent
facets.meaning: Knowing one's own accent and individual sound, the base for accent work, and declaring the native accent to casting.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School audition panel (stage 1 self-tape)
Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles

facets.name: Accents You Can Really Do
facets.meaning: Only accents done convincingly count: casting may call on any listed, and a drama-school panel warns against an accent the actor is not confident in.
judges: Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles
RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (speech choice, on its list of things not to do)

facets.name: Learning A Dialect
facets.meaning: Using the tools and systems for learning and performing a dialect, in training or with a dialect coach.

facets.name: Accent Clips
facets.meaning: Short recorded clips of each accent, so casting directors who search by accent can hear it; a range of accents opens film and voice work.
judges: Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles

facets.name: The Accent The Role Needs
facets.meaning: The accent a casting call asks the actor to prepare for the character.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines)

covers.name: Speak different languages
covers.definition: Speaking one or more foreign languages well enough to read a script in them and take on a varied repertoire.

facets.name: Reading A Script In It
facets.meaning: A working command of the language, enough to read a script in it and make sense of it, not a tourist’s phrases.
judges: Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles (a casting director’s view)

facets.name: A Native Language For Authenticity
facets.meaning: A native language, clearly marked, for roles that need one spoken authentically.
judges: Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles

facets.name: A Wider Repertoire
facets.meaning: A foreign language mastered to take on a more varied repertoire, which the French actor diploma attests.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien assessment (RNCP38358)

facets.name: Work Abroad
facets.meaning: More languages, more chances of being cast in productions outside one’s own country.

facets.name: The Production's Language
facets.meaning: Performing in the language the production works in: auditions accept a piece from another language but want it in English, and a fully dubbed performance loses Oscar eligibility.
judges: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, acting branch (eligibility)
Guildhall School BA Acting audition panel
RADA admissions panels

covers.name: Voice-over (incl. home studio)
covers.definition: Performing with the voice alone for recorded media, from commercials and animation to audiobooks and games, in a studio or a home setup.

facets.name: Radio, Commercials, Audiobooks, Animation And Games
facets.meaning: The range of voice work: radio drama, commercials, audiobooks, animation, narration and game voice acting.

facets.name: Microphone Technique
facets.meaning: The studio craft: microphone technique, control of breath, volume and inflection, and working with the director, producer and engineers in the booth.

facets.name: Home Studio
facets.meaning: Having a home studio, or access to one, and a quiet recording space, which casting directors want listed.
judges: Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles

facets.name: Voice Reels And Demos
facets.meaning: Recorded voice reels and demos for casting directors to hear, worth posting only if they are good.
judges: ACTRA Toronto voice performer database
Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles (a casting director’s view)

facets.name: Character Voice Performance
facets.meaning: Portraying a character with the voice alone, which the Emmys reward in a category of its own, closed to on-screen performers’ categories.
judges: Television Academy (Emmy Awards), Category 75

covers.name: Singing
covers.definition: Using the voice to produce musical sounds, marked by tone and rhythm, and performing and interpreting a song.

facets.name: Tone, Rhythm And Range
facets.meaning: The voice as a singing instrument: its tone, rhythm, range and musicality, practised on a song's lyrics, melody and rhythm.
judges: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, acting branch (eligibility)
Juilliard Drama Division faculty (Actor Training Program audition)

facets.name: Acting The Song
facets.meaning: At a drama-school audition the song is judged as acting: connecting to its language and playing its human situation, not technical singing.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting audition panel

facets.name: Voice Type And Range
facets.meaning: The voice type and range a singer truthfully lists, with clips, so casting can search for it.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines), musical theatre
Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles

facets.name: The Song Call
facets.meaning: Bringing songs in different styles and tempos, choosing one that suits the style and shows the range, agreeing tempo with the pianist, and singing solo, with an accompanist or unaccompanied.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines), musical theatre
David Geffen School of Drama at Yale, Acting Audition Committee (callbacks)

covers.name: Speaking
covers.definition: Talking to others to convey information effectively: speaking clearly so others understand, communicating at work, and talking about the show and your own choices.

facets.name: Conveying Information
facets.meaning: Talking to others to share information effectively.
judges: O*NET 27-2011.00 Actors

facets.name: Speaking Clearly
facets.meaning: Speaking clearly, communicating ideas so others understand.

facets.name: Speaking At Work
facets.meaning: Communicating verbally and non-verbally with professionals and laypeople at work.
judges: NAST accreditation, BFA in Acting

facets.name: Talking About The Show
facets.meaning: Addressing audiences about the show, sharing your creative approach and opening up the work.

facets.name: Explaining Your Choices
facets.meaning: Talking about your pieces, the play and your creative decisions in an interview or audition.
judges: NIDA audition video panel

actor.name: Physicality
actor.definition: Dance, Perform stunts, Appropriation d'espace scénique, Clown, Make-up technique and Special skills.

covers.name: Dance
covers.definition: Studying and practising the dance moves a production needs, at the standard and in the style its choreography asks.

facets.name: Learning The Combination
facets.meaning: Picking up and performing the moves a production requires, as taught at a dance call, after which there may be a cut.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines), musical theatre

facets.name: Style And Standard
facets.meaning: The styles one can dance and at what level, honestly stated; productions set their own standard, from basic period dance to musical theatre.
judges: Casting directors searching Spotlight profiles
Managers (producers) auditioning under the Equity/SOLT West End Agreement

facets.name: Period Dance
facets.meaning: Dances of a period, learned with period movement and stage combat to understand period texts.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School assessment (MFA, pass/fail)

facets.name: The Body As Instrument
facets.meaning: A trained, controlled body, through dance and movement, that serves characterisation and answers changing rhythms and spatial relationships.

covers.name: Perform stunts
covers.definition: Preparing and performing physical action such as stunts and fights for film, television and stage, with the training, and the qualified people on set, that safety requires.

facets.name: Action Stunts
facets.meaning: Preparing and performing the physical movements a difficult action scene needs, learned as directed like lines and cues.
judges: O*NET 27-2011.00 Actors

facets.name: Stage And Screen Combat
facets.meaning: Fencing, stage combat and choreographed fight sequences across genres.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School MFA Professional Acting

facets.name: Safety And Qualified Supervision
facets.meaning: Working to the safety rules, with someone trained in that stunt engaged and on set, and never made to do a stunt without consulting them.
judges: SAG-AFTRA Codified Basic Agreement

facets.name: Stunt Work Recognised
facets.meaning: Stunt work done under a stunt contract and on camera, listed with stunt databases and honoured by the awards.
judges: Television Academy (Emmys)
The Actor Awards

covers.name: Appropriation d'espace scénique
covers.definition: Making any playing space your own: adapting to its features and constraints, mastering body, movement and space, and fitting the voice to the venue.

facets.name: Owning Any Space
facets.meaning: Making any playing space your own, from a theatre stage to a public place or a library.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien (RNCP38358)

facets.name: The Space’s Constraints
facets.meaning: Playing inside the allotted space with its features, technical constraints and configuration.

facets.name: Body, Movement And Space
facets.meaning: Controlling speed, agility and flow of movement and your relation to the space, responsive to spatial relationships.
judges: RADA BA Acting audition panel, movement session

facets.name: Voice To The Venue
facets.meaning: Adapting voice to the acoustics and size of the place so the text carries.
judges: Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines

facets.name: Space And The Other Actors
facets.meaning: Adapting to the space and to the other actors in it.

covers.name: Clown
covers.definition: Clown as a theatre discipline of actor training, for risk-taking, play and physical storytelling, and as comedy routines in clown costume and make-up.

facets.name: Clown Training
facets.meaning: Clown studied as a discipline of the actor's art in drama school.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School BA (Hons) Professional Acting

facets.name: Risk-Taking And Play
facets.meaning: Clowning to take risks and play.
judges: Yale Summer Conservatory for Actors

facets.name: Physical Storytelling
facets.meaning: Clown explored alongside physical storytelling and embodied performance.

facets.name: Extending Your Register
facets.meaning: Drawing on neighbouring arts such as clown, mask and puppetry to widen your playing register.

facets.name: Clown Routines
facets.meaning: Performing comedy routines in clown costume and make-up.

covers.name: Make-up technique
covers.definition: A working knowledge of make-up materials and techniques: applying and touching up your own make-up, as an artistic choice for the character, alongside the make-up crew.

facets.name: Applying And Touching Up
facets.meaning: Putting on and refreshing your own make-up with the right techniques.

facets.name: Make-Up As Artistic Choice
facets.meaning: Applying make-up as the artistic choice for the role requires.
judges: NAST accreditation, BFA in Acting

facets.name: Make-Up Calls And Crew
facets.meaning: Working with the make-up crew, keeping make-up calls and adapting make-up in rehearsal.

facets.name: Clown Make-Up
facets.meaning: Comic clown make-up and costume for comedy routines.

covers.name: Special skills
covers.definition: Every skill you can do well and convincingly, such as accents, languages, instruments, singing voice, dance styles, sports, riding, combat or driving, listed so casting searches can find you.

facets.name: Listed So Casting Finds You
facets.meaning: Every skill listed on your profile, where casting searches it to meet a brief.
judges: Casting directors on Spotlight

facets.name: Only What You Can Deliver
facets.meaning: Listing only what you can show at a professional level, at its true proficiency.
judges: Casting directors (Spotlight)

facets.name: Highly Skilled
facets.meaning: Marking the few things you are truly highly skilled at, which casting can filter for.
judges: A casting director on Spotlight

facets.name: Shown On A Reel
facets.meaning: A clip or specialist reel that shows the skill.

facets.name: Skills Roles Call For
facets.meaning: The skills productions ask for and that make a character authentic: accents, languages, instruments, singing, dance, riding, combat, driving, voice-over.

actor.name: Camera
actor.definition: Acting for the camera and Self-taping.

covers.name: Acting for the camera
covers.definition: Acting to the technical demands of a film set, continuity, marks, eye lines and lens sizes, while telling the story believably on screen.

facets.name: Continuity, Marks, Eye Lines And Lenses
facets.meaning: The technical demands of a set: keeping continuity, hitting marks, holding eye lines, knowing the lens size, and managing energy and concentration.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting, Screen 1 assessment (On Screen Exercise, pass/fail)

facets.name: Believable On Screen
facets.meaning: Conveying a clear story and believability on camera, often through small adjustments.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting, Screen 2 assessment (self-tape exercise)

facets.name: The Through-Line Out Of Sequence
facets.meaning: Keeping the story's through-line while scenes are shot out of order, in a screenplay's own form and language.

facets.name: Playing To The Reader, Not The Lens
facets.meaning: Facing the camera without looking into it, playing to the reader beside it, held in a tight frame.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines), self-tapes

facets.name: Watching Playback
facets.meaning: Reviewing one’s own takes on playback as part of the work, with taping help and feedback available to union members.

covers.name: Self-taping
covers.definition: Recording your own audition tape to casting's brief and to industry norms: seen and heard clearly, framed and lit well, acted truthfully, often with a reader and on a short turnaround.

facets.name: Lighting, Sound And Framing
facets.meaning: The technical side of the tape: you can be seen and heard clearly, lit from behind the camera, framed in landscape.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting, Screen 2 module
NIDA audition video panel

facets.name: The Acting On Tape
facets.meaning: The screen acting itself: eyeline off the lens, to a person beside the camera, without overthinking the takes.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting, Screen 2 module

facets.name: On Your Own, To Industry Norms
facets.meaning: Taping efficiently and independently, anywhere, to what the industry expects.

facets.name: Quick Turnaround
facets.meaning: Learning and taping the pages within the turnaround casting sets, sometimes at the last minute.

facets.name: A Reader
facets.meaning: Taping with someone reading the other lines.

facets.name: Following The Brief
facets.meaning: Taping exactly to the casting director's instructions or the set brief.
judges: NIDA audition video panel

actor.name: Direction
actor.definition: Ability to take direction, Rehearsal with a director, Ensemble ethos, Collaborative ethos, Improvisation and Adaptability.

covers.name: Ability to take direction
covers.definition: Following the director's instructions while understanding their creative vision, and changing the work in response to notes.

facets.name: What The Director Wants
facets.meaning: Understanding the director's creative vision and what they expect of the actor, and building one's own reading from their instructions.

facets.name: Changing On A Note
facets.meaning: Taking a note and changing the work in response, which drama-school panels test by working on a speech with a director.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School MFA audition (two staff)
NIDA BFA (Acting) recall
RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (short workshop)
RADA admissions panels

facets.name: Keeping The Note
facets.meaning: Recording a direction and sustaining it through every rehearsal and performance, not only the next take.
judges: RADA BA Acting (Hons) module assessment

facets.name: What You're Like To Work With
facets.meaning: How the actor listens to notes and responds, and asks when a note is unclear, which tells the director what they will be like to work with.
judges: Casting directors and directors (Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines)

covers.name: Rehearsal with a director
covers.definition: Preparing a performance in rehearsals led by a stage or screen director, working on the role with the director, the dramaturg and the company.

facets.name: Rehearsing Under The Director
facets.meaning: Preparing the performance through rehearsals under the director's instruction, deepening the work on the character together.

facets.name: The Read-Through
facets.meaning: Reading the script together with the director and company to lay down the main lines of the roles.

facets.name: Staging Rehearsals
facets.meaning: Finding gesture, expression and movement in staging rehearsals, and building the character's physical path with the director's intentions.

facets.name: Taking And Keeping Direction
facets.meaning: Receiving, recording and sustaining the director's notes, and reproducing in performance the choices fixed in rehearsal.
judges: RADA BA Acting audition, short workshop with a director

facets.name: Different Directors’ Ways
facets.meaning: Working across a range of rehearsal approaches, as an active contributor to the process.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting

facets.name: Shared Exploration
facets.meaning: Taking part in the group's research and improvising in rehearsal with directors, fellow actors and writers to find the role.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien (RNCP38358)

covers.name: Ensemble ethos
covers.definition: Working as one of a company: giving an individual performance that stays connected to the ensemble, and sustaining an ensemble way of working.

facets.name: Individual Yet Connected
facets.meaning: A performance that is the actor's own and at the same time tied to the whole company, without giving up individuality.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien assessment (RNCP38358)

facets.name: Listening To The Others
facets.meaning: Listening to what the others do and staying aware of the people, space, set and objects shared on stage, committed to the joint work.

facets.name: Building And Sustaining The Company
facets.meaning: Creating and keeping up an ensemble way of working with the other actors, a core task of the job.
judges: RADA BA Acting (Hons) module assessment
The Actor Awards presented by SAG-AFTRA

facets.name: In Support Of The Group
facets.meaning: Committing to the group work and developing skills in support of the others, working creatively in response to them.
judges: RADA BA (Hons) Acting audition panel (full workshop day)
RADA admissions panels

covers.name: Collaborative ethos
covers.definition: A disposition to work with others: committing to the shared work, supporting and listening to partners, and communicating with the ensemble, the director and the other disciplines.

facets.name: Committing To The Shared Work
facets.meaning: Committing to the collaborative nature of the work for its whole length.
judges: RADA BA Acting audition panel, full workshop day
Yale (David Geffen School of Drama) Acting Admissions Committee

facets.name: Supporting Others
facets.meaning: Listening actively, contributing and supporting the others in the group.
judges: NIDA interview and callback panel

facets.name: With Director, Actors And Writers
facets.meaning: Working closely with director, fellow actors and playwrights, attuned to and reacting to partners.

facets.name: Across Disciplines And Crew
facets.meaning: Communicating and collaborating with other disciplines and the crew.
judges: NIDA BFA (Acting)

facets.name: Ensemble Working Ethos
facets.meaning: Creating and sustaining an ensemble ethos with generosity, respect and inclusion.

facets.name: Listening And Negotiating Ideas
facets.meaning: Listening to others' opinions and putting forward and arguing proposals in a way that earns trust.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting assessment criteria

covers.name: Improvisation
covers.definition: Performing dialogue or action spontaneously, without preparation, alone or with others, and to a given brief.

facets.name: Making It Up On The Spot
facets.meaning: Inventing dialogue or action in the moment, without preparing it, which casting advice values for creativity and spontaneity.
judges: Directors who build part of a production from improvisation (as Spotlight reports)

facets.name: Improvising With Others
facets.meaning: Improvising effectively both alone and in a group, which drama schools test in group sessions at audition and recall.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School MA Screen Acting recall panel
Bristol Old Vic Theatre School audition panel (BA recall)
Guildhall School BA Acting audition panel

facets.name: Improvising To A Brief
facets.meaning: Improvising a role, or to instructions given, using known improvisation techniques.

facets.name: Improvising For Camera And Auditions
facets.meaning: Using improvisation to make small, telling adjustments in a screen audition and to be at ease with the script and character.

covers.name: Adaptability
covers.definition: Being open to and comfortable with change: adapting the performance to changes and short notice, adapting in the room, and adapting to the needs of the profession.

facets.name: Open To Change
facets.meaning: Comfort with change, new experiences and ideas at work.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting assessment criteria
O*NET 27-2011.00 Actors

facets.name: Changes In The Run
facets.meaning: Adapting the performance to changes on tour or when a show is revived.

facets.name: Short Notice And Script Changes
facets.meaning: Coping with last-minute tapes, short-notice material and script changes on set.

facets.name: Physical And Vocal Adaptability
facets.meaning: Adapting body and voice to what the text, the character and the director ask.
judges: RADA BA Acting audition, short workshop with a director

facets.name: Adapting In The Room
facets.meaning: Adapting in the moment to people, tasks and ideas in the room.
judges: NIDA interview and callback panel

facets.name: Adapting To The Profession
facets.meaning: Handling varied, changing work situations and a profession that keeps changing.

actor.name: Auditioning
actor.definition: Prepare for and go to auditions, Audition technique, Promote yourself, Organiser et développer son réseau professionnel and Personal organisation.

covers.name: Prepare for and go to auditions
covers.research: prepare for and go to auditions
covers.definition: Preparing for and attending auditions and casting calls: reading the whole play, preparing exactly what was asked, knowing the material well, and turning up on time.

facets.name: Going Up For Roles
facets.meaning: Attending auditions and casting calls, often put forward by an agent.
judges: O*NET 27-2011.00 Actors

facets.name: Reading The Whole Play
facets.meaning: Reading the whole script to understand character, relationships and context.

facets.name: Preparing What Was Asked
facets.meaning: Preparing exactly the scenes, accent, song or physical work asked for, and asking if unclear.

facets.name: Choosing Audition Pieces
facets.meaning: Preparing contrasting, fully memorised pieces for a school audition.

facets.name: Familiar With The Material
facets.meaning: Knowing the sides well enough that your head is not in the script, and arriving fully prepared.
judges: Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines

facets.name: Mock Auditions
facets.meaning: Practising auditions and interviews with feedback before the real thing.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting, Industry Preparation module

facets.name: Recalls And Callbacks
facets.meaning: Coming back for recalls and callbacks, warming up, singing and reworking the pieces with the panel.
judges: Yale (David Geffen School of Drama) Acting Admissions Committee

covers.name: Audition technique
covers.definition: The craft of the audition room: cold reading, working with the reader, taking notes, pitching to the room, saying the lines as written, and introducing yourself and the piece.

facets.name: Audition Training
facets.meaning: Coaching and workshops in audition technique and the actor's audition procedures.
judges: NAST accreditation, BFA in Acting

facets.name: Cold Reading
facets.meaning: Reading new or short-notice material well with the script in hand.

facets.name: Taking Notes In The Room
facets.meaning: Listening to the director's notes and showing how you respond.
judges: Casting Directors' Guild audition guidelines

facets.name: Working With The Reader
facets.meaning: Playing the scene with whoever reads in, and agreeing any physical contact first.

facets.name: Lines As Written
facets.meaning: Saying the text as written, without approximations or verbal tics.

facets.name: Room, Voice And Props
facets.meaning: Pitching the voice to the room and keeping props and mime to what helps the scene.

facets.name: Introducing Yourself And The Piece
facets.meaning: Slating your name and introducing each piece by character, play and author.

covers.name: Promote yourself
covers.definition: Marketing your own strengths in skills and knowledge, and making your work known to agents, casting directors and the networks that fit your career plan.

facets.name: Headshot, CV And Reels
facets.meaning: A professional headshot, CV, showreel and voice reel ready to put in front of agents and casting directors.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting, Industry Preparation module

facets.name: A Profile Casting Can Find
facets.meaning: A directory profile kept full and current, so that casting searches find you and you stand out.
judges: Casting directors searching Spotlight

facets.name: Marketing Your Strengths
facets.meaning: Selling what you can do, with a clear view of the market you mean to work in.
judges: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School MFA Professional Acting

facets.name: Making Your Work Known
facets.meaning: Telling the right networks and platforms what you are working on now.

facets.name: Showcasing To Industry
facets.meaning: Performing in a showcase that agents and casting directors are invited to watch.
judges: Agents at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland showcases

facets.name: Promoting Your Art
facets.meaning: Taking part in promoting the show and your art, speaking with the public about it.
judges: France compétences RNCP28105 (inactive)

covers.name: Organiser et développer son réseau professionnel
covers.research: Organiser et développer son réseau professionnel
covers.definition: Keeping up and growing lasting personal and professional relationships with theatres, production companies, agents and professional bodies, to get new work.

facets.name: Lasting Relationships
facets.meaning: Keeping up personal and professional networks through relationships that last, including with professional organisations.
judges: Ministère de la Culture DNSP Comédien (RNCP38358)

facets.name: Contacts That Bring Work
facets.meaning: Staying in touch with theatres, production companies and employers to land the next job.

facets.name: An Agent
facets.meaning: Taking on, and negotiating with, an agent who puts you forward for auditions and castings.

facets.name: Meeting The Industry
facets.meaning: Meeting directors, agents, casting directors and producers and building visibility and useful contacts.

facets.name: Keeping Up With The Profession
facets.meaning: Following the profession's news and press, at home and abroad.

covers.name: Personal organisation
covers.definition: Organising your own work and priorities for a demanding, irregular schedule: setting goals, managing workloads, meeting deadlines, and arriving on time and prepared.

facets.name: Organising Your Own Work
facets.meaning: Setting goals and priorities, managing workloads and meeting deadlines.
judges: QAA Subject Benchmark Statement: Dance, Drama and Performance

facets.name: A Demanding Schedule
facets.meaning: Coping with intense, discontinuous work, evening and weekend calls, odd hours and frequent travel.

facets.name: On Time And Prepared
facets.meaning: Arriving in good time and fully prepared, and telling casting at once if delayed.
judges: Equity UK Code of conduct for auditions

facets.name: Time, Resources And Accountability
facets.meaning: Managing time and resources, preparing thoroughly and seeing work through to completion.
judges: Guildhall School BA Acting assessment criteria

facets.name: Keeping Your Kit Ready
facets.meaning: Preparing and maintaining the instrument, props and gear the performance needs.
